- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., 0.00 or -0.33) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward drag or lagged mean reversion to prevent overextension.
- In high-event periods (e.g., >18 events/30d, net supply negative), model underestimates downside risk — increase downward bias or add volatility penalty to forecast.
- If sentiment is bullish but price declines sharply (e.g., 5%+ drop from prior day), model often fails to adjust — add downward momentum filter or sentiment-weighted correction.
- In low-event or neutral sentiment windows, model tends to drift upward — apply downward drift correction or use recent 7-day mean as baseline.
- When supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model often ignores supply shock — add supply-weighted downward adjustment to forecast.
- If model forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows early sharp drop (e.g., 3–5 days), apply early correction rule: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until trend reversal.
- In multi-day auction periods (e.g., 3+ consecutive auctions), model often overestimates price stability — apply downward volatility buffer or add auction-specific decay factor.
